questions.question: Describe the lower course of a river and explain why flood plains are important.
questions.expected_answer: Lower course: widest, deepest channel, largest volume, very gentle gradient near base level; little erosion except in floods; fine load in suspension; deposition dominant. Flood plain: wide flat land flooded regularly; each flood deposits silt, building fertile alluvium; meanders, oxbow lakes and scars. Supported early civilisations (Nile, Tigris-Euphrates, Indus, Yellow River). Few large flood plains in SA because rivers are short and steep (examples: Pongola, lower Orange).

questions.question: Explain how natural levees form and evaluate the use of artificial levees.
questions.expected_answer: In a flood, water leaves the channel, becomes shallow and slows sharply (friction), losing energy; coarse sand and silt deposited next to the channel, finer silt/clay further away; repeated floods build raised ridges along both banks; bed may also rise (Yellow River flows above plain). Artificial levees/dykes protect land (Mississippi) but confine floods, increase downstream flooding, stop silt reaching the plain, and can fail catastrophically (New Orleans, Hurricane Katrina 2005, about 80% flooded, over 1 800 deaths).

questions.question: Explain how deltas form, describe types of deltas and the benefits and risks of living on them.
questions.expected_answer: River enters still/slow water, slows and deposits; flocculation in sea water; sediment builds up to the surface; river splits into distributaries. Needs heavy load, weak waves/tides/currents, shallow shelf. Types: arcuate (Nile, about 240 km coast), bird's-foot (Mississippi), cuspate (Tiber); inland delta (Okavango, World Heritage 2014). Benefits: fertile alluvium, flat land, water, fishing, ports, wetlands/mangroves (Sundarbans); Ganges-Brahmaputra largest. Risks: floods, cyclones and storm surges, sinking, sediment trapped by dams (Aswan, 1970), sea-level rise. SA has few deltas due to strong waves/currents and narrow shelf; estuaries instead.
